source.title: Polynomial Speedup in Diffusion Models with the Multilevel Euler-Maruyama Method

record.file_problem: The text is readable, with minor formula and OCR/formatting artifacts; it is not an abstract-only or wrong-document extract.
record.tranche_reason: The paper extends scaling-law evidence to image diffusion: it reports a power-law fit for denoising error against UNet evaluation time on CelebA images. It does not test the language-model loss or compute-optimal allocation claims.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling-law results from other studies as motivation; those cited results are not rows. Its ML-EM sampling speedup comparisons are results about the proposed sampler, not measurements of the claim versions. Figure 2 supplies the relevant result.
record.test_reason: The paper's own Figure 2 fits denoising error (minus a hand-chosen 0.15 offset) against evaluation time for UNet diffusion models of increasing size on CelebA 64×64. It reports a log-log slope of about −0.4. This is a result on whether a power-law form holds for image diffusion models (V5). The rest of the paper concerns sampler speedups and does not bear on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. ML-EM needs only about one largest-network evaluation's worth of compute when γ>2. For DDPM it gives up to roughly 4× less compute at equal MSE, or about 10× lower MSE at equal time. The advantage for DDIM is 'less clear, but still present'. The authors estimate γ≈2.5 on CelebA 64×64 and expect larger speedups at industrial scale.
record.recipe_differences: Measures image-model denoising error against evaluation time, with a manually chosen error offset; it does not reproduce language-model held-out-loss scaling or the original parameter/token/compute measurements.
record.problems: The scaling fit is from one small image dataset and a range of five UNets; the error offset was chosen by hand to align the points. No uncertainty estimate or comparison across alternative offsets is reported. The paper also notes that it does not have access to the true score.
record.rows_left_out: Cited scaling-law findings from references [8], [10], and [12] are not the paper’s own results. The reported ML-EM-versus-EM generation-time and MSE comparisons in Figure 1 concern sampler performance, not the claim versions, so they are not rows.

untested.parts: Video and other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer. Scaling in parameters or data, as opposed to evaluation time. Any range beyond five small UNets on one 64×64 dataset.
Extrapolation to larger runs; not tested.
Architecture shape at fixed size; not tested. Width and depth vary together across the UNets.
No comparison of fitting choices. The offset choice affects the exponent but alternative offsets are not reported.

record.verdict_notes: The scaling-law fit is incidental to the paper; it serves to estimate γ for choosing sampler probabilities. The cited image scaling exponents from Henighan et al. ([8]) are not the paper's own results and correctly are not rows. Single-author preprint, run on two consumer GPUs.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss of language models versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether fits on small language-model runs predict much larger runs.
The compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Architecture effects at fixed parameter count.

Tests one image-diffusion setting, using denoising error against evaluation time rather than language-model held-out loss. Video, repeated-data training, fine-tuning, transfer, and other modalities or regimes are not tested.
Downstream-task performance or its predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
No systematic comparison of fitting choices, setups, published exponents, compute-optimal splits, or departures from a single power law.

rows.subject: UNets f¹, f², f³, f⁴, f⁵
rows.size_stated: Increasing sizes; the text lists base dimensions 8, 16, 32, 64 for the networks.
rows.stage_stated: Each network trained separately on the usual denoising loss
rows.operation_detail: Fit denoising error minus 0.15 against UNet evaluation time across a range of network sizes.

conditions.value: Subtract 0.15 from denoising error; offset chosen by hand

rows.measure: Denoising error versus evaluation time; reported log-log slope and implied γ
rows.value: The plot fits well with ϵ ∼ t⁻⁰·⁴; γ ≈ 2.5.
rows.note: One reported fit across the range of UNets; the text says the 0.15 offset was chosen to make the plotted points align as closely as possible to a line.
rows.check: size_stated is incomplete. The text names five networks (f1–f5) but gives only four base dimensions (8, 16, 32, 64), depths L1 = 5, 10, 20, 40 and L2 = 2, 3, 5, 7, so one network's size is unstated. The x-axis is evaluation time, a compute proxy, not parameter count. The error offset was hand-tuned to make the points line up, which partly builds the linearity into the fit. It is unclear whether the denoising error is held-out or training error. No exponent uncertainty or goodness-of-fit is given. 'Observed' rests only on the author's statement 'fits well'.

relationships.condition: CelebA 64×64 image diffusion; five small UNets (f1–f5); denoising error minus 0.15 against evaluation time
relationships.reason: Log-log fit ϵ∼t^−0.4, stated to fit well (r1). The evidence is weak: only five points, a hand-chosen offset tuned for linearity, and no uncertainty reported.
relationships.display_finding: Denoising error minus 0.15 fitted ϵ∼t^-0.4 across five UNets, using an offset chosen for linearity and without reported uncertainty.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.condition: CelebA images downscaled to 64 × 64; denoising error versus evaluation time for the tested UNets
reader_labels.reason: The reported fit is a power law with slope −0.4 and implied γ ≈ 2.5 (r1), supporting the power-law form in this image-diffusion setting.
